primary_users.description: Primary operator who owns the workspace, configures vendors, runs imports, reviews Discovery Sessions, curates the catalog, and controls what enters inventory.
motivations: Unify vendor product and service data into one owned catalog
Stop manual copy/paste between vendor pages and internal systems
Control what enters inventory with review before import
Use AI without being locked to a single provider
success_criteria: Can import from website, PDF, and manual entry with one workflow
Can curate and edit catalog items fully after import
Can produce flyers and quotes from owned catalog data
Can switch AI providers without losing catalog data

secondary_users.description: Future user invited to a workspace to collaborate on catalog, discovery, and outputs once team support ships.
success_criteria: Can work within an invited workspace

secondary_users.description: Configures workspace-level AI settings (API keys, provider selection, capability routing) and monitors provider health.
motivations: Connect one or more AI providers
Route AI capabilities to the best or cheapest provider
Keep provider configuration isolated from business logic
success_criteria: Can register and swap providers via adapter configuration
Can route capabilities (catalogExtraction, semanticSearch, etc.) without code changes
Can run the platform with zero providers configured

user_goals.goal: Aggregate vendor products and services into one curated catalog
Review imported candidates before they become catalog items
Produce business outputs (flyers and quotes) from owned catalog data
Track vendor and document changes across imports over time
Use any AI provider interchangeably for enrichment and extraction
Configure AI provider adapters and capability routing at workspace level

user_needs.need: Bulk actions for discovery and catalog editing
Responsive UI that does not block during long scraping or AI jobs
Manual entry that is as capable as automated import
evidence_refs: System-References/PRD Docs/Source Blender PRD.md#Core Product Principles

user_needs.need: Transparent vendor change history (price, description, new/removed items)

user_system_relationships.relationship: Reviews candidate items, edits before import, ignores or archives candidates
Owns, edits, and curates catalog items after import
Produces business outputs from owned catalog data
Configures providers and capability routing; monitors health
Triggers imports and reviews sync history

role_or_permission_hints.notes: V1 likely ships single-role workspace owner until team support is added.
Future; no team workflow target in MVP.
May overlap with workspace_owner in V1.

stage_decision_brief.recommended_direction: Build Source BlendR as an AI-agnostic Vendor Intelligence Platform: multi-tenant workspaces, Playwright-first website discovery, PDF catalog extraction, Discovery Session staging before import, Universal Catalog Items (products, services, rentals, labor, manufacturing, installation), AI Provider Adapter Architecture with capability routing, background workers, and deferred future features per the PRD.
alternatives_considered: Single AI provider only (rejected: violates AI-agnostic locked principle)
Auto-import without Discovery Sessions (rejected: violates discovery-before-import locked principle)
Product-only catalog (rejected: violates Universal Catalog Items locked decision)
Plug-in marketplace architecture (rejected: explicitly out of scope in Inference Layer summary)
key_decisions: Playwright is the locked web discovery engine
AI is provider-agnostic via adapter architecture and capability router
Discovery Sessions always gate catalog imports
Universal Catalog Items replace Product-only schema
Manual entry is a first-class workflow; platform runs with zero AI providers
Background workers handle scraping and AI processing
PDF imports are equal in status to website imports
Flyer and Quote Builders are should-have; may be trimmed or deferred to protect MVP risk

assumptions.assumption: Playwright + AI-assisted site analysis handles the majority of target-market vendor sites.
Target users value provider independence and owned catalog data.
Discovery Sessions are accepted as friction-positive vs auto-import competitors.
Universal Catalog Items cover the target market without forcing partial re-architecture.
Background workers keep the UI responsive for expected scrape/AI durations without a streaming UI.

risks.description: Playwright reliability across diverse vendor sites
Target market too small or unwilling to pay

downstream_impact: Stage 2 must validate differentiation hypotheses, market demand, and technical assumptions (Playwright reliability, OCR/AI extraction quality, Universal Catalog schema coverage).
Stage 3 must lock adapter interface, capability router contract, validation engine contract, multi-tenancy isolation boundary, and queue/timeout strategy.
Stage 4 must validate Discovery Session UX and catalog browsing UX.
Stage 5 slices import-to-catalog flow, adapter architecture, and catalog as launch-critical; flyer/quote as should-have.
Stage 6 acceptance criteria must include AI extraction-quality tests per capability and validation engine tests.
